title: Curve testing for geometric irreducibility
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq1$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $X_0$ whose
geometric restrictions to $X$ are irreducible local systems. Let $S$ be
a nonempty finite set of $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-points of $X$. There
are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains $S$,
such that every $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$,
and $C$ is defined over a finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$:
there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with
$i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where
$\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius of
$X$.

proof.text: On the geometric fibre, smooth base change supplies relative dimension d; the fibre is affine and connected. For d>=2 apply the pro-etale detector to the geometric carriers, obtaining one connected finite etale cover whose connected restriction to a smooth connected affine curve detects all irreducibility conditions.

Apply the existing Bertini theorem to that cover and the prescribed geometric points. It supplies a closed smooth connected affine curve through every point and connectedness of the restricted cover, as well as the positive Frobenius power and its curve automorphism. The detector gives simultaneous irreducibility of all pulled-back carriers. Return the Bertini witnesses and this conclusion.

If 2<=d fails, positivity forces d=1. Take the whole geometric fibre with its identity immersion, m=1, and its geometric Galois Frobenius. Identity pullback is isomorphic to each original carrier, so irreducibility is unchanged; every prescribed point factors through the identity.

proof_origin.place: Bertini assembly and the final dimension-one sentence, with the finite-quotient argument isolated in lem-zl-proetale-irreducibility-detector.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq1$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $X_0$
(lisse $\QbarX$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]
with a Weil structure [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]) whose
geometric restrictions to $X$ are irreducible local systems. Let $S$ be
a nonempty finite set of $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-points of $X$. There
are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains $S$,
such that every $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$,
and $C$ is defined over a finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$:
there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with
$i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where
$\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius of
$X$.

proof.text:
Use the geometric representations of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation]. By
[thm-lisse-qlbar-representations], each is a continuous representation
of $\pi_1(X)$ defined over some finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$
inside $\Qlb$; enlarging $E$, one $E$ serves for all of them. As in
[p-real-integral], compactness of $\pi_1(X)$ gives a stable
$\mathcal O_E$-lattice in each, i.e. a basis in which all matrices have
entries in $\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility],
applied with $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_E$, each has a finite
reduction quotient detecting absolute irreducibility. Intersect
their open normal kernels in $\pi_1(X)$, where
$X=X_0\times\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. The resulting finite quotient
$Q$ corresponds to a connected finite etale Galois cover $T\to X$.
For $\dim X\geq2$, apply
[lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve]. Connectedness of the
restricted $Q$-torsor means that the image of $\pi_1(C)$ acts
transitively on $Q$, hence is all of $Q$. It surjects onto each
chosen reduction quotient. The finite matrix witnesses show that
all the restricted geometric representations remain irreducible.
The curve and inclusion descend to a finite constant extension;
the restrictions inherit their Weil structures over that field.
For dimension one take $C=X$, with its given finite-field model.
